answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 244 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is recorded against the tide challenge, the pearl audit can replay the quill history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm thus has to pad 137 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
